Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.testElementDOM calls doTestElement(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM).
  - doTestElement delegates to doTest("/ElementA/B:ElementB", model, "MY VALUE").
  - doTest builds a JXPathContext over a DocumentContainer created from ExternalNS.xml, registers namespaces A -> "foo" and B -> "bar", and asserts that evaluating the XPath returns "MY VALUE".
  - createDocumentContainer(model) constructs a DocumentContainer on the XML and explicitly sets namespace awareness to false. A comment notes this setting only works for DOM, which is the model used here.

- The intended scenario:
  - The XML contains elements with prefixes (e.g., A:..., B:...) but without in-document namespace declarations.
  - The test relies on “external” namespace mappings provided via context.registerNamespace("A", "foo") and context.registerNamespace("B", "bar").
  - Because the XML lacks namespace declarations, the DOM must be parsed with namespace awareness disabled so the parser will accept prefixed element names literally (nodeName like "B:ElementB", no namespace URI/local name).

- Where the mismatch occurs:
  - XPath compilation produces a name test for B:ElementB with namespace URI "bar" and local name "ElementB".
  - The DOM nodes (parsed with namespace awareness disabled) expose:
    - node.getNamespaceURI() == null
    - node.getLocalName() == null
    - node.getNodeName() == "B:ElementB"
  - Matching logic in the DOM model (DOMNodePointer and related name test handling) compares the compiled QName (namespace URI "bar", local "ElementB") against the DOM node’s namespace and local name. Because the DOM node’s namespace URI is null (due to non-namespace-aware parsing), the match fails.
  - The implementation does not correctly fall back to using the nodeName’s prefix ("B") and resolving it through the context’s registered namespaces when the DOM node itself is namespace-unaware.

- How this ties to the bug report:
  - The report “Incomplete handling of undefined namespaces” describes failures when dealing with prefixes that are not defined in the parsed document (e.g., attributes causing “unknown namespace prefix: xsi” in DOMNodePointer.createAttribute).
  - The same root cause applies here: when namespaces are not defined in the document (because the parser is non-namespace-aware and/or the XML doesn’t declare them), the code fails to use the externally registered namespaces for name resolution and matching.
  - For elements, this leads to selection failure (hence testElementDOM failing).
  - For attributes (as in the report), it manifests as an exception when attempting to create or resolve an attribute with an external prefix.

- Conclusion:
  - The DOM model’s namespace resolution for non-namespace-aware nodes is incomplete. When DOM parsing is namespace-unaware, the code should:
    - Split node.getNodeName() into prefix/local components if a colon is present.
    - Resolve the prefix using the JXPathContext’s namespace resolver to obtain a namespace URI.
    - Use that derived namespace/local name during matching against the compiled XPath QName.
  - This fallback is missing or only partially implemented (likely implemented for some cases but not for attributes, and currently failing for element matching in this scenario), leading to the test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.testElementDOM calls doTestElement(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM).
  - doTestElement delegates to doTest("/ElementA/B:ElementB", model, "MY VALUE").
  - doTest builds a JXPathContext over a DocumentContainer created from ExternalNS.xml, registers namespaces A -> "foo" and B -> "bar", and asserts that evaluating the XPath returns "MY VALUE".
  - createDocumentContainer(model) constructs a DocumentContainer on the XML and explicitly sets namespace awareness to false. A comment notes this setting only works for DOM, which is the model used here.

- The intended scenario:
  - The XML contains elements with prefixes (e.g., A:..., B:...) but without in-document namespace declarations.
  - The test relies on “external” namespace mappings provided via context.registerNamespace("A", "foo") and context.registerNamespace("B", "bar").
  - Because the XML lacks namespace declarations, the DOM must be parsed with namespace awareness disabled so the parser will accept prefixed element names literally (nodeName like "B:ElementB", no namespace URI/local name).

- Where the mismatch occurs:
  - XPath compilation produces a name test for B:ElementB with namespace URI "bar" and local name "ElementB".
  - The DOM nodes (parsed with namespace awareness disabled) expose:
    - node.getNamespaceURI() == null
    - node.getLocalName() == null
    - node.getNodeName() == "B:ElementB"
  - Matching logic in the DOM model (DOMNodePointer and related name test handling) compares the compiled QName (namespace URI "bar", local "ElementB") against the DOM node’s namespace and local name. Because the DOM node’s namespace URI is null (due to non-namespace-aware parsing), the match fails.
  - The implementation does not correctly fall back to using the nodeName’s prefix ("B") and resolving it through the context’s registered namespaces when the DOM node itself is namespace-unaware.

- How this ties to the bug report:
  - The report “Incomplete handling of undefined namespaces” describes failures when dealing with prefixes that are not defined in the parsed document (e.g., attributes causing “unknown namespace prefix: xsi” in DOMNodePointer.createAttribute).
  - The same root cause applies here: when namespaces are not defined in the document (because the parser is non-namespace-aware and/or the XML doesn’t declare them), the code fails to use the externally registered namespaces for name resolution and matching.
  - For elements, this leads to selection failure (hence testElementDOM failing).
  - For attributes (as in the report), it manifests as an exception when attempting to create or resolve an attribute with an external prefix.

- Conclusion:
  - The DOM model’s namespace resolution for non-namespace-aware nodes is incomplete. When DOM parsing is namespace-unaware, the code should:
    - Split node.getNodeName() into prefix/local components if a colon is present.
    - Resolve the prefix using the JXPathContext’s namespace resolver to obtain a namespace URI.
    - Use that derived namespace/local name during matching against the compiled XPath QName.
  - This fallback is missing or only partially implemented (likely implemented for some cases but not for attributes, and currently failing for element matching in this scenario), leading to the test failure.
